scenes.heading: Handling clients who want to pay after publishing instead of upfront

sents.d: Handling clients who want to pay after publishing instead of upfront
Payment terms are a negotiation, not something to just accept because a client proposed it.

A client proposing payment only after their content is published (rather than on delivery) shifts real risk onto you — the content is finished and delivered, but payment depends on their own timeline or decisions, which you don't control.

A standard structure — deposit at start, balance on delivery of the final draft, regardless of when they choose to publish — protects your income without being an unreasonable ask; most professional clients expect this.
If a client pushes back hard on standard payment terms specifically, that's often a useful early signal about how the rest of the working relationship will go.

take: Get paid on delivery, not when they decide to publish.
